Describe the photograph's framing, then classify it for extracting a COMPLETE isolated fashion product.
Choose ONE view label:
FLAT_LAY: whole product(s) alone on a surface, with their outside outline visible.
PRODUCT_ONLY: whole product(s) alone, e.g. hanging or invisible mannequin.
WORN: any actual person or body part wearing, holding or modelling the item. Printed portraits on fabric are not actual people.
DETAIL: fabric texture fills the frame, or only a subsection such as a neckline, sleeve, fastening or hem is shown. A fabric rectangle is NOT a whole garment. Close-up detail shots never count as flatlays.
OTHER: visible mannequin, unrelated scene or uncertain.
For FLAT_LAY or PRODUCT_ONLY, list the visible product types in items. For any clothing garment include the word "clothing" (so the entire garment, including all attached layers, can be segmented), plus its plain type, such as "dress", "shirt", "vest". For jewellery, shoes or bags use those specific object names. List ALL items of a pair/set. For WORN, DETAIL or OTHER items must be [].
Return ONLY a JSON object with exactly these keys: description (a brief explanation of visible framing), view (one label above), items (list of strings).

reference_type_evidence.raw:
```json
{
  "description": "A black bikini top with small embellishments is displayed against a white background.",
  "view": "FLAT_LAY",
  "items": ["bikini top"]
}
```

selection.reason: A black bikini top with small embellishments is displayed against a white background.
